newsitem.title: JAPAN: Majority of big Japan electric firms shun Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Majority of big Japan electric firms shun Nomura.

text.p: Six out of the nine major Japanese electric power companies have excluded scandal-hit Nomura Securities Co Ltd from underwriting their bond issues, officials at the companies said on Friday.

Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) said it barred Nomura from participating in the underwriting of its 50 billion yen 12-year straight bond on Thursday. Nomura had been a member of the syndicate for TEPCO's previous issue in April.

"Our stance is that until monetary authorities have decided what measures to take (in the Nomura affair), we have asked Nomura to refrain from being part of the syndicate," said Kazuhiro Hasegawa, a TEPCO spokesman.
"Our decision after that will depend on what moves are taken by the monetary authorities."

Although Nomura was a syndicate member when Chubu Electric Power Co Inc issued its last straight bond on April 14, five of Japan's nine major electric companies have excluded Nomura from the syndicates for all the bonds they have issued since April, when Japan's new fiscal year began.
The five firms are Tohoku Electric Power, Hokuriku Electric Power, Chugoku Electric Power , Kansai Electric Power and Shikoku Electric Power.
Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc's April issue was for wholesale investors, so it excluded Nomura, but Nomura took part in the syndicate for a more recent issue this month.
"We decided to include Nomura in the syndicate for the issue of straight bonds out of consideration for the convenience of individual investors in our area," a company official said.
He added that the company was waiting for the decision of monetary authorities before deciding about later issues.
Hokkaido Electric Power has not launched any straight bonds since the start of this fiscal year.

Nomura is embroiled in a scandal involving payoffs to racketeers that broke in March. A former president of the firm was arrested on Friday over the scandal, for which the company faces as yet undetermined administrative penalties.
It has lost many other corporate clients since the scandal broke.
